# Carlos Alcaraz and Marc Márquez Take Spanish Sports to the Top


by[Press](https://nomadar.com/author/press/)


| Nov 23, 2026


|[News](https://nomadar.com/category/news/) |[0 comments](https://nomadar.com/carlos-alcaraz-and-marc-marquez-take-spanish-sports-to-the-top/#respond)


Carlos Alcaraz and Marc Márquez have given Spanish sports another reason to celebrate. For Nomadar and Cádiz CF, they are two examples of talent, hard work, and consistency, the same values that are worked on every day in the HPT (High Performance Training) program.


On Sunday, Alcaraz won his first ATP Finals title in Turin, beating world number one Alexander Zverev in the final 6-2, 7-6(7). With this win, he becomes the third Spaniard to lift the trophy, after Manuel Orantes in 1976 and Àlex Corretja in 1998, ending a 28-year wait.


He did it after a season marked by doubts and physical problems. In Turin, he showed he can still compete at the highest level. At only 23, he already has seven Grand Slam titles and six titles in 2026, and his numbers are starting to compare with those of the greats of tennis.


That same Sunday, Marc Márquez was crowned MotoGP world champion and won his tenth world title, his eighth in the premier class, after coming back from a 102-point deficit. It is another example of determination from the rider from Cervera, who had already returned to the top last year after his serious injury in 2020.


They are two different sports, but one way of competing. Both have shown that talent needs hard work, patience, and the ability to get back up when things do not go as expected. That is also the idea behind the HPT (High Performance Training) program of Nomadar and Cádiz CF, where players from all over the world, between 12 and 18 years old and between 18 and 21, come to train, live, and study in Spain.


Spanish sports have been adding big names for years, and Alcaraz and Márquez show that the list keeps growing. Behind these results is a way of understanding sports that starts at the grassroots level, with good training and a lot of work. It shows in soccer, tennis, motorcycle racing, and padel, where Spain’s men’s and women’s national teams recently won the World Championship.


In the HPT (High Performance Training) program of Nomadar and Cádiz CF, players who come from different countries do not just train. They also learn to work hard, to never give up, and to keep going when something goes wrong. Seeing champions like Alcaraz and Márquez is one more motivation for them, and one more reason to keep backing talent and Spanish sports.
